inferred_framework: Drupal (server-rendered, with heavy custom JS and GTM/dataLayer integrations; no evidence of Next.js, React root, Angular, or Vue markers).
narrative: Navigation proceeds linearly from the Nasdaq homepage to a COMP index page, then to the AAPL quote page and its dividend history, historical prices, and historical NOCP subpages, all on www.nasdaq.com. Every page shares a common Drupal 10-based layout with meta[name=Generator]=Drupal 10, consistent header/footer, a global symbol search form (/symbol-search with langcode=en and q), a watchlist-add overlay form, a full-site search overlay form, and several generic textarea-field__form POST forms likely used for tagging or feedback. Hidden inputs are minimal and limited to a static langcode=en field; no CSRF tokens are visible in meta tags or hidden inputs, suggesting CSRF protection is either cookie-based, handled via AJAX headers, or embedded in dynamically loaded JS rather than in the captured DOM. Structured data is provided via JSON-LD on all pages, describing the Nasdaq corporation, the current WebPage with breadcrumbs, and the WebSite search action, while large Drupal settings JSON blobs and digitalData/dataLayer objects capture page identity, breadcrumbs, timestamps, user/session attributes, and JWT-like inzAhTk tokens per page for internal APIs and analytics. Tables across the capture are mostly skeleton loaders for charts, key data, historical data, recently viewed, and trending symbols, with only a few concrete data tables visible (homepage curated symbol tables, retail activity tracker table, and AAPL bid/ask and ETF holdings tables). The frontend framework is best characterized as Drupal-driven server-side rendering with rich client-side enhancements via custom JavaScript, Google Tag Manager, Adobe DX/chatbot scripts, OneTrust consent scripts, and mPulse performance monitoring, but without clear SPA framework signatures like __NEXT_DATA__, data-reactroot, ng-* attributes, or Vue data-v-* attributes.
